description: Spec-Driven Development with organizational governance. Specs tell AI agents what to build; Charter governs how they build it. Git-native missions, enforceable workflows, and consistent engineering standards across AI coding agents and harnesses.
vibe: Governance-first engineering where the charter outranks the code and every shortcut is a defect waiting to ship.
highlights: Charter-first mandate: every agent must load .kittify/charter/charter.md before planning, and the charter wins any disagreement with AGENTS.md.
Pack tier firewall: packs/built-in ships to consumers, packs/internal never does, with a packaging safety test guarding the boundary.
Canonical sources only: never copy structure from older missions or hand-roll CLI equivalents; trace and file upstream gaps instead.
Retired-surface discipline: Team Kitty is frozen, sync identifiers are residue, and no # noqa: TID251 for retired modules.
Calibrated test policy: run your blast radius, never whole-repo suites, and record commands plus counts in the PR.
assessment: This file treats agent instructions as a constitutional layer rather than a style guide, which is unusually mature for AI-assisted development. The explicit precedence rule (charter beats AGENTS.md, flag drift instead of silently resolving it) prevents the classic failure mode where agents improvise around ambiguity. The built-in versus internal pack split, backed by a packaging test, shows the team understands that doctrine leakage to consumers is a real defect class, not a documentation nit.
